title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the neighbouring pages. G is a group scheme with a 'determinant' character δ_G. The examples have the shape of GL_2: there is a torus T_0 ⊂ G with δ_G : T_0 ≅ G_m, so G ≅ T_0 ⋉ SG. ε_0 is a regular unipotent section, giving a root-type subgroup L_0 = ε_0(G_a) ⊂ SG. ρ and σ are central sections of commutative group schemes T_ρ and T_σ. Notation: x(y) = int(x)(y) = x y x^{-1} and [x,y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1}.

Hypotheses used on this page:
- (158a): b^{-1}σ(b) = ε_σ(b), i.e. b(σ) = ε_σ(b)·σ.
- (159b): T_0 normalises L_0 and acts on it through det, i.e. u(ε_0(λ)) = ε_0(μλ) with μ = det u.
- σ^{-1}ρ ∈ ε_0·T_0, and ε_1 = σ(ε_0).

The unknown U is written U = f^{-1}u with f ∈ SG and u ∈ T_0. Put α = u a^{-1}, β = u b^{-1}, α_0 = f^{-1}α, β_0 = f^{-1}β.

Step 1: (160) becomes (161), where f no longer appears:
- u(ρ) = int(α)(ρ). This is tautological, since int(a^{-1})ρ = ρ because T_ρ is commutative.
- u(σ) = ε·int(β)(σ). This reduces to int(u)(σ), using b^{-1}(σ) = ε·σ from (158a).
Grothendieck remarks that proving (160) used only (158a) and (159b).

Step 2: he now wants to derive the 'relation des lacets' (157) formally, noting he must already have done this calculation two or three times in slightly different contexts.
- (161bis): u(ε_0) = ε_0(μ), so [u, ε_0] = ε_0(μ−1).
- Also [u, ε_0] = u·ε_0(u)^{-1}, and ε_0(u)^{-1} is rewritten via σ^{-1}ρ(u). Hence σ([u, ε_0]) = σ(u)ρ(u)^{-1}.
- Put ξ = [u,ρ] = αρ(α)^{-1} and η = [u,σ] = εβσ(β)^{-1}. Then ρ(u) = ξ^{-1}u and σ(u) = η^{-1}u.
- So σ[u, ε_0] = η^{-1}u·u^{-1}ξ = η^{-1}ξ.
- Applying σ to [u, ε_0] = ε_0(μ−1), with σ(ε_0) = ε_1, gives η^{-1}ξ = ε_1(μ−1).
- That is, αρ(α)^{-1} = εβσ(β)^{-1}·ε_1(μ−1). This is the loop relation (157), the same shape as (158b): [u,ρ] = [u,σ]ε_1(μ−1).

Purpose: to show that the loop equation's solution scheme M_{ρ,σ} can be described, under the structural hypotheses (158a) and (159b), by the simpler normalised equations (160)/(161). The next page summarises this as a Proposition, (162)–(165).
errors: Minor and self-corrected: Grothendieck crosses out a stray ε in the second line of (161) and several false starts in the commutator manipulation. The final derivation is consistent.
In the step ε_0(u)^{-1} = (σ^{-1}ρ)(u)^{-1}, he tacitly uses σ^{-1}ρ ≡ ε_0 modulo T_0, together with commutativity of T_0. This is fine, but left implicit.
The conventions x(y) = xyx^{-1} and [x,y] = xyx^{-1}y^{-1} are never stated. He notes 'attention aux signes' on the previous page. Under these conventions the result checks out.

ideas.what: Torus T_0 ≅ G_m via det acting on a regular unipotent one-parameter subgroup through the determinant character; splitting G = T_0 ⋉ SG.
ideas.modern_name: Borel subgroup / root subgroup of GL_2; semidirect decomposition GL_2 = G_m ⋉ SL_2
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (general theory of reductive group schemes)

ideas.what: Formal commutator calculus deriving the 'relation des lacets' αρ(α)^{-1} = εβσ(β)^{-1}ε_1(μ−1) from normalised equations (161).
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian cocycle / twisted-conjugacy identity in a group scheme
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure — specific to Grothendieck's 'équation des lacets' programme
ideas.where_published: Related material in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981), not published in this form

ideas.what: Reduction of the loop-equation moduli M_{ρ,σ} to equations independent of the SG-component f (U = f^{-1}u).
ideas.modern_name: Gauge fixing / normal form for a torsor under T_0 ⋉ SG

deep.surprise_reason: A routine verification step: a formal commutator calculation that Grothendieck himself says he has done several times before. It belongs to the unpublished 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', but this page contains no new idea or connection beyond the internal bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: The image reads [u, ε_0] = ε_0(μ−1) (μ minus 1), not ε_0(μ^{-1}). Likewise the final line is η^{-1}ξ = ε_1(μ−1), i.e. ξ = η ε_1(μ−1).
'u(φ)' should be 'u(ρ)', and 'T_φ commun.' should be 'T_ρ commutatif' (the ρ is misread as φ).
'U = f^{-1}u' in the first line: the left side is U (capital), not u.
The definition of η should read η = ε β σ(β)^{-1} (σ, not ρ), consistent with (160).
The crossed line reads approximately 'ρ u ρ^{-1} u^{-1} = ξ'. The final margin note reads 'i.e. (157) OK!'.
Line 1 is 'Les deux autres formules (160) s'explicitent', not '(159)'.
In the paragraph text, 'dans des contextes qui ne différaient que par le fait à moi' is unclear in the image; it plausibly reads 'qui ne différaient que fort peu'.
